claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles with a uniform, few-nanometer graphene layer creates an engineered nanoscale graphene interlayer at tungsten/copper interfaces.
A graphene interlayer at tungsten/copper interfaces enhances interfacial thermal coupling.
The ultrathin graphene coating reduces thermal resistance at tungsten/copper interfaces.
The graphene interlayer promotes efficient phonon transport between tungsten and copper.
The graphene interlayer promotes efficient electron transport between tungsten and copper.
Graphene has high intrinsic thermal conductivity.
Graphene has robust intrinsic mechanical properties, including high strength and modulus.
Graphene's mechanical properties help preserve tungsten/copper interfacial integrity under mechanical stress.
Graphene's mechanical properties help preserve tungsten/copper interfacial integrity under irradiation.
Tungsten has high intrinsic thermal conductivity that can be more effectively coupled to the copper matrix through the graphene interlayer.
Graphene-coated tungsten particles increase the effective thermal conductivity of a W–Cu composite relative to an otherwise comparable composite containing uncoated tungsten particles.
The graphene-coated W–Cu composite retains mechanical strength comparable to the uncoated W–Cu control.
The graphene-coated W–Cu composite retains irradiation resistance comparable to the uncoated W–Cu control.
The predicted benefits apply under elevated temperatures, cyclic thermal loads, and moderate irradiation exposure typical of heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint applications.
The predicted benefits depend on the graphene coating being continuous, intact after processing, and maintained at an optimal few-nanometer thickness.
A nonuniform or excessively thick graphene coating may negate the thermal and mechanical benefits.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity enhancement may vary with coating quality and processing parameters.
